data.text:
Use a token-bucket rate limiter keyed by client IP. It allows short bursts while enforcing a sustained request rate and is more suitable than a fixed window’s boundary spikes.

Place it in `src/server.ts` after `express.json()` and before `app.use("/notes", notesRouter)`, so every Notes endpoint is protected while `/` remains available as a health check.

Default limit: 60 requests per minute per IP, with a burst capacity of 20 requests. Make these values configurable via environment variables.

When limited, respond with HTTP `429 Too Many Requests`:

```json
{
  "error": "Too many requests",
  "retryAfter": 12
}
```

Also include a `Retry-After` header containing the number of seconds until another request is likely to succeed.

# demo-app

A small Notes API used as a demo project for ctrlyoke workflow captures (screenshots/GIFs).
Deliberately minimal — just enough existing structure for a workflow to extend.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path         | Description         |
| ------ | ------------ | -------------------- |
| GET    | `/notes`     | List all notes       |
| GET    | `/notes/:id` | Get a single note    |
| POST   | `/notes`     | Create a note         |
| DELETE | `/notes/:id` | Delete a note        |

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run dev    # start with live reload
npm test       # run the test suite
```

you find real issues, then summarize your review findings in a short
paragraph.

data.text: The review found two concrete edge-case improvements: wall-clock rollback could reduce a client’s token balance unexpectedly, and the default key should fall back to the socket address before grouping truly unidentified requests together. I’m also tightening numeric option validation; the in-process state is synchronous and safe within one Node event loop, but a multi-worker deployment would still need shared storage for a global limit.

data.text:
Review complete. The limiter safely handles concurrent clients within a Node process, isolates them by IP/socket address, and fails closed when no client identity is available. I fixed clock-backward handling by clamping negative elapsed time and validated invalid numeric configuration values. Its state remains process-local, so multi-worker deployments would require shared storage for a global limit.

`npm test` and `npm run build` both pass.
